sections.h2: Where to record a deed in Wilmington
sections.html:
Real estate recording is handled in Land Records, Suite 102, at 320 Chestnut Street in Wilmington. A second counter on Government Center Drive accepts recordings in the afternoon only.

  • Land Records, Suite 102 (main office), 320 Chestnut Street, Wilmington, NC 28401: Monday through Friday, 8 to 5.
  • Vital Services, Suite 120 (same building): Monday through Friday, 8 to 5.
  • Satellite office, 230 Government Center Drive, Wilmington, NC 28403: recording from 2 pm to 5 pm on weekdays, vital records from 8 am to 5 pm.

The office number is 910-798-4530. Anything sent by mail must go to the Suite 102 address, never the satellite site.

sections.h2: What the county wants on page one
sections.html:
Quite a bit. On top of the statewide format rules, Wilmington's office requires these items on recordings:

  • A return name and address for the original document.
  • The drafter's name, on every deed and deed of trust.
  • The parcel's tax ID number, on any document that conveys land.
  • The grantee's address, again on conveyances of land.

Tax ID numbers come from Land Records in the county Tax Department, at 910-798-7300. Get the number early, since it has to be typed onto the deed before anyone signs.

The county will still record a deed that breaks the format rules, for an extra $25.00 under G.S. 161-10(a)(19) on top of ordinary fees. To avoid it, follow this list when you file in Wilmington.

  • Page sizes: 8 1/2 by 11 or 8 1/2 by 14 inches.
  • Margins: three inches blank at the top of page one, half an inch elsewhere on that page, and half an inch on every side of later pages.
  • Ink and font: black on white, with 9 points counted as the smallest legible size.
  • Sides: text on the front of the sheet only.
  • Label: the instrument type at the top of page one, outside the blank margin.

Blanks may be inked in by hand, and corrections must use black ink. Releases of deeds of trust or mortgages, in every form, and UCC filings are exempt from these standards.

The fee schedule for fiscal year 2026-27, revised July 1, 2026, sets the charges below. Plats and maps have their own lines, and a deed that must be re-indexed under later instruments can draw extra index fees.

The same schedule charges $10 for a notary oath and $5 for a notarial act.

The rate is $1.00 per $500.00 of price, which works out to $2.00 per $1,000.00. State law makes the seller pay, and G.S. 105-228.30 requires payment at the register before recording.

If you call and ask what a house sold for, you will be told only the stamp amount. The Register does not search titles or report on liens.

The schedule also shows the rate by era: $2 per $1,000 from 1991 to the present, $1 per $1,000 from 1968 to 1991, and $1.10 per $1,000 before 1968. That helps if you read an old deed and wonder what its stamp meant.

sections.h2: What the register can and cannot do
sections.html:
The office keeps the public record but cannot advise you on it.

  • Off limits: legal advice, attorney referrals and title searches.
  • Public: every filed record except DD-214 discharges, open to viewing and copying at the office.
  • Name changes on title: a new deed is needed to add or drop a name.
  • Wills: filed with the Estate division of the Clerk of Superior Court.
  • Maps: subdivision and condominium plats only, not lot surveys.
  • House size and age: ask the Tax Department.

A free fraud alert is available too. Once you enroll, any document recorded under your name triggers an email with a copy. Owners of a vacant or inherited house may want it.

sections.h2: Why does the order of recording matter?
sections.html:
Under G.S. 47-18, the first instrument registered takes priority, and a deed that was never registered gives no protection against lien creditors or buyers who paid value. A deed signed on Friday but filed the following week can lose to something registered in between.

Because the office does not run title searches, ask an attorney or title company to check for open liens before anything is signed.

sections.h2: Other services at the Wilmington office
sections.html:
Besides land records, staff issue certified vital records, passport services and military discharge filings, and they take e-filed assumed business name certificates. Marriage licenses need an appointment, while notary oaths do not.

The county's page also links a public records search and a guide called "Don't Overpay for a Copy of Your House Deed," useful when a closing needs a copy of the vesting deed. First-time adult passport books are $165 and passport cards $65. Certified birth, death and marriage copies are $10 each, a marriage license is $60, and a minor's passport book is $135. Mailed requests for uncertified vital record copies carry a $1.25 fee. For a business-name form, the office keeps printed copies of the Secretary of State form as a courtesy.

Before listing, get a copy of your vesting deed and note the tax ID, the drafter and the grantee address that the county expects on page one. Ask your closing attorney whether a release of your current deed of trust is queued, since satisfactions record without a fee. If you are selling to a cash buyer, the same recording steps apply to the deed, but there will be no new deed of trust to file.

New Hanover County has 128,402 housing units, and owners live in 61.4% of occupied homes, so a large share of buyers and sellers are landlords or investors who file frequently. Arriving with a correct deed saves a second trip downtown. Bring a pen with black ink for any fill-ins, and confirm the hours for the counter you plan to visit, since the satellite office records only in the afternoon. Mail goes to Suite 102 on Chestnut Street, so allow a few days for delivery before a closing deadline.

faqs.q: What is the street address for recording a deed in Wilmington?
faqs.a: Go to 320 Chestnut Street, Suite 102, in Wilmington (ZIP 28401). A satellite counter at 230 Government Center Drive takes recordings from 2 pm to 5 pm on weekdays.

faqs.q: Will New Hanover County accept a deed by mail?
faqs.a: Yes, but only at the Suite 102 address on Chestnut Street. Mailed recordings should not go to the satellite office.

faqs.q: Who owes the New Hanover County excise tax?
faqs.a: The seller. The rate is $1.00 per $500.00, and the register can later tell you only the stamp amount on the recorded deed.

faqs.q: Where can I find my parcel's tax ID for a New Hanover County deed?
faqs.a: Ask Land Records at the county Tax Department, 910-798-7300. The number belongs on page one next to the grantee's address.

faqs.q: Are wills filed with the New Hanover County register?
faqs.a: No. They go to the Estate division of the Clerk of Superior Court. The register handles deeds and other property records.
